title: Pixel 11 battery drain could have an unexpected culprit: Your Wi-Fi router
summary: Tests point to a router-specific sleep issue, but the cause isn't confirmed.
body: TL;DR Some Pixel 11 owners are reporting excessive idle battery drain, with Wi-Fi showing unusually high battery usage. A detailed test found that certain routers repeatedly woke the phone, preventing it from sleeping properly. Switching to Wi-Fi 5 or another router dramatically improved battery life, but the exact cause remains unconfirmed. Pixel owners are no strangers to battery-life complaints , and Google’s Tensor era has had its share of heat, modem, and efficiency problems. The Pixel 11 series looked like a step forward, especially with its new MediaTek modem, but some owners are now chasing a different kind of drain. A detailed Reddit investigation suggests certain Wi-Fi routers may be keeping Pixel 11 phones awake far more often than they should. Reddit user Albamen13 noticed their Pixel 11 Pro XL losing roughly 2.5% to 3% battery per hour while sitting idle on Wi-Fi. Using BetterBatteryStats, they found that Wi-Fi activity was waking the phone about 135 times per minute, preventing it from properly going to sleep for 59% to 67% of the test.

title: Gmail just made copying 2FA codes much less annoying
summary: A new inbox shortcut lets you grab verification codes without opening emails.
body: TL;DR Gmail is rolling out a “Copy code” button for two-factor authentication emails on Android and iOS. The shortcut lets you copy a verification code directly from your inbox without opening the email. The feature is appearing in Gmail for Android version 2026.09.07.x and iOS version 6.0.260907, but not on the web yet. Gmail has already made email easier to navigate this month with Live voice features and Gemini-powered inbox answers , and now Google is shaving another few seconds off a common task. Gmail is rolling out a new “Copy code” shortcut that lets you grab a 2FA code straight from the inbox without opening the message first. While two-factor authentication is supposed to keep your accounts safer, the last step can still feel unnecessarily clumsy when the code lands in your inbox. This shortcut is here to address that, and it appears as a pill-shaped “Copy code: 000000” button beneath the email’s subject line, in the same area Gmail uses for attachment previews and other contextual actions.

title: No RCS, no problem: Chat themes in Messages are now available for standard texts
summary: You can now set wallpapers and your favorite colors for conventional text messages.
body: TL;DR Google Messages is quietly rolling out the ability to set custom chat themes for standard SMS conversations. Chat themes were previously limited to RCS chats in the messaging app. This change may have been facilitated by chat themes being limited to the person who set it rather than everybody in the conversation. While Google Messages has long let users customize their RCS chats with a selection of colors, it got a major upgrade in August with the introduction of chat themes, a feature we first uncovered in May . One key limitation of this customization tool is that it only works with RCS chats. It now looks like Google has flipped the switch for standard SMS/texts, too. As a Reddit user points out , Google Messages appears to have quietly enabled chat themes for non-RCS chats. A quick look on my Pixel 6a confirms this, with a red dot prompting users to try it for the first time.

title: The Pixel Weather widget now lets you catch up on the forecast with a single tap
summary: The update also removes unnecessary buttons hogging space in the app.
body: Credit: Rita El Khoury / Android Authority TL;DR Google is updating the Pixel Weather app again with subtle changes. The update adds a refresh button on the home screen widgets. It also removes the arrow buttons that let you scrub hourly and daily weather predictions left or right. The Pixel Weather app is one of the finest options for anyone who likes (or needs) to keep track of weather trends frequently. In addition to its gripping visuals, the Pixel Weather app offers a wide range of data to satisfy your appetite for details, while also delivering a custom AI summary that helps you plan ahead for upcoming journeys to other locations. Since the app is already quite palatable, there’s little room for improvement, but product engineers at Google keep striving to add subtle changes to keep your experience engaging . The latest set of changes arrives in the form of a tiny button to update the current weather on the home screen widget. While the Pixel Weather app refreshes actively when you open the app, the widget only updates in the background at certain intervals. Before the update, users had no control over when or how frequently the widget would update.

title: That security patch date on your Android phone is no longer the full story
summary: Google has released new tools allowing Android apps to get a much more accurate picture of how secure your phone really is.
body: Credit: Rita El Khoury / Android Authority TL;DR Google’s new Security State libraries let apps check the security status of individual Android components instead of relying only on the overall security patch level. Apps can also check whether a security update is available and ready for installation, potentially prompting users before they perform sensitive tasks. A phone can now be recognized as protected even if its overall security patch date hasn’t changed, as long as it has received the specific security fix. Until now, your Android phone’s security patch level and the date attached to it have served as an easy way for apps and businesses to check whether your phone is up to date. But it doesn’t always tell the complete story.
